newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on IMF, Yeltsin news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on IMF, Yeltsin news.

text.p: MinFin bonds firmed on Monday on news the International Monetary Fund approved disbursement of delayed funds from its loan to Russia and President Boris Yeltsin's meeting with his security chief, dealers said.

"The tone of the market is bullish, because of the IMF news and the fact that Yeltsin is meeting Rybkin," said said Moscow Business World dealer Sergei Kovzharov. "However, there is no agressive demand."
The IMF board on Friday approved disbursement of over $650 million from its $10 billion loan to Russia.
Yeltsin, still convalescing from pneumonia at a country residence outside Moscow, met security chief Ivan Rybkin there on Monday.

Kovzharov said the low demand was due to a fall in U.S. Treasuries after a meeting of finance ministers and central bankers of the Group of Seven industrialised countries at the weekend agreed major currency misalignments had been corrected.
Sergei Seryogin, an Aljba-Alliance dealer, said Moscow banks did most trading with the biggest activity in tranches 4 and 5.
Kovzharov forecast a bullish market this week with tranche 6 hitting 50.00, tranche 7 rising to 37.00, tranche 5 to 44.00 and tranche 4 to 63.00 at bids.
"Without bad news the market has real chances to firm further," Seryogin said.
